Russian Missiles Attack Kyiv Overnight, Fires Reported in Sviatoshynskyi and Obolon — Russian forces attacked Kyiv with missiles in the early hours of Thursday, with falling debris causing fires in the Sviatoshynskyi and Obolonskyi districts. Authorities also reported a blaze at a garage cooperative, while the Air Force warned of missiles heading toward Kyiv, Dnipro and Kryvyi Rih.

Ukraine to End VAT Exemption on Imported Goods Bought via Foreign Marketplaces — Ukraine’s government has approved a bill that would end value-added tax (VAT) exemptions for imported goods bought through foreign marketplaces. Authorities say the move could bring in more than Hr. 10 billion (roughly $223.3 million) a year and would not take effect before 2027.

Ukrainian F-16 Fighter Jet Crashes During Combat Mission — The Air Force of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) reported losing contact with an F-16 fighter jet during an ongoing combat mission on Wednesday, July 29, after an in-flight emergency forced the pilot to eject. The pilot was evacuated safely, with no civilian casualties reported.

Russia to Launch a Massive Strike Tonight, AFU Warns — President Volodymyr Zelensky warned that Russia is expected to launch a massive strike on Ukraine tonight, following days of preparation by Russian armed forces. He urged the US and other partners with Patriot systems to act quickly to help protect civilians.

Zelensky Meets Tusk in Lublin, First Poland Visit Since Diplomatic Fallout — President Volodymyr Zelensky met Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk in Lublin on Wednesday, July 29, to discuss defense cooperation, anti-ballistic missile priorities, and the protection of Ukrainian refugees in Poland. The meeting marked Zelensky’s first visit to Poland since the two countries’ diplomatic fallout over a military unit’s honorary UPA title in June.

France to Deport Pro-Kremlin Journalist Fedorova, Puts Her Under House Arrest — France has ordered Xenia Fedorova, former head and editor-in-chief of RT France, the French branch of Russian state-backed network RT, to leave the country over allegations of spreading Kremlin propaganda on French television and radio. She has been placed under house arrest and must report daily to the police.
Putin’s Donbas Offensive Just Backfired — Putin still wants the last fortress cities of Donbas. However, that is a trap that will quickly lead to the unravelling of the Putin Regime.

Ukraine Appeals IOC Decision to Ease Restrictions on Russia — Ukraine has appealed to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) after the International Olympic Committee (IOC) eased restrictions on Russian athletes, saying that the decision was premature and breached the Olympic Charter.

5 Things to Know About the Russia Sanctions Bill: Looks Tough, Lots of Carve-Outs Baked In — The bill Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia Act of 2026 (S. 5025) is a bipartisan plan for new laws aimed at strengthening US sanctions on Russia and third parties doing business with it. EU Clusters for Dummies: Where Ukraine Stands — Ukraine has formally opened two of the EU’s six accession negotiation clusters, moving its membership bid from political declarations to detailed talks. But slow reform implementation, government reshuffles, and continued Hungarian resistance could complicate Kyiv’s ambition to join quickly.

‘This Is No Laughing Matter’: Lavrov Says Entire West Has United Against Russia, Warns of Its ‘Dismemberment’ — Sergei Lavrov claimed the West had united against Russia, sought to “dismember” the country and was issuing Moscow ultimatums over the war in Ukraine.

New Przemysl-Frankfurt Train to Start Operating on Aug. 1 — Spanish operator is launching a new route between the Polish-Ukrainian border city of Przemysl and Germany’s Frankfurt am Main on Aug. 1. The train starts from €27.5 ($31) and takes around 19 hours, while passing through the Czech Republic.

SBU Strikes Major Russian Oil Refinery 1,500 km From Ukraine — The Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) announced on Wednesday that it successfully struck the Lukoil-Permnefteorgsintez oil refinery, located more than 1,500 km from Ukraine. The refinery, one of Russia's largest with a capacity of nearly 13 million tons per year, supplies fuel to both civilian and military sectors.

Writing on Wall for Putin in D.C. — Timothy Ash argues that Washington’s growing bipartisan support for tougher Russia sanctions, Ukraine’s battlefield gains and drone warfare edge are shifting the dynamics of the war. He says mounting pressure could push Vladimir Putin toward negotiations as the Kremlin faces rising economic and military challenges.

Russian Window to Attack Europe: NATO Won’t Be Ready Until 2035 — The United States has formally warned Poland that Russia may stage an armed provocation on its soil within months – designed to test NATO’s Article 5 commitment and force the West to halt aid to Ukraine. To understand why this warning matters, start in 1967.

Poland: Opposition Party PiS Collapses — Poland’s opposition party PiS has split after more than 30 MPs left following a leadership dispute between Jarosław Kaczyński and former Prime Minister Mateusz Morawiecki. Commentators say the split could reshape Polish politics, weakening Donald Tusk’s main rival, while critics argue Morawiecki lacks credibility due to his role in PiS’s controversial reforms and policies.

Zelensky Asks Trump for 300 Patriot Missiles Before Winter — In an interview with Axios, Zelensky said he asked Trump for an emergency package of 300 Patriot missiles before the winter season, as Ukraine's stockpiles are almost depleted and the country cannot defend against Russian ballistic missiles without them.

Majority of Poles Oppose Backing Ukraine’s EU Bid, Poll Finds — The survey found that 52% of Poles oppose supporting Ukraine’s EU membership efforts, while 65% reject sending Polish troops to oversee a postwar ceasefire. On military assistance, 44% favored suspending support over the UPA dispute, compared with 41% who wanted it continued.

Iran Considered Missile Strike on Ukrainian Port After Caspian Sea Ship Attack – NYT — Iran reportedly considered launching a symbolic ballistic missile strike on a Ukrainian seaport after Ukraine hit an Iranian vessel in the Caspian Sea, but backed down following diplomatic pressure. Tehran later said it did not seek escalation while demanding compensation for the attack.

Russia Weighs State Support for Wildberries After Ukraine Strikes — The Kremlin is exploring financial support for Wildberries after Ukrainian drone attacks damaged its warehouses, disrupting operations and affecting thousands of businesses that rely on the retailer.

Russia Hints at Mobile Catapult Launchers for S8000 'AliExpress' Cruise Missiles — Photos circulating in Russian media show what appears to be a Banderol missile mounted on a catapult launcher on display, with the missile previously known only to be air-launched by the Orion drone and Mi-28 attack helicopters. Ukraine previously warned that Russia has used more Banderols in recent attacks, which also has a smaller turn radius than other Russian cruise missiles.

‘More Air Strikes on Russian Forces for Victory’ Drapaty Tells NATO Chief in 1st Call — Ukraine's Commander-in-Chief Mykhailo Drapaty spoke with NATO's Supreme Allied Commander Europe, outlining battlefield priorities and thanking the United States for continued military assistance.

Russia Declares Telegram Founder Pavel Durov an International Fugitive Over Terrorism Charge — Russian authorities charged Telegram founder Pavel Durov with facilitating terrorist activity and placed him on an international wanted list. The FSB linked the allegations to Telegram content it claims was used by Ukrainian intelligence services

Wildberries Eyes Kazakhstan Warehouses After Ukrainian Drone Strikes Hit Russian Logistics Network — Russia’s largest marketplace, Wildberries, is seeking warehouse space in Kazakhstan after Ukrainian drone strikes hit its logistics facilities in Russia. The company is reportedly looking for up to 100,000 square meters of storage capacity to shield part of its supply chain from further attacks.

Iran Says It ‘Does Not Seek Escalation’ After Sybiha Call Over Caspian Sea Strike, Demands Compensation — Iran says it does not seek escalation with Ukraine after a rare high-level call between the two countries’ foreign ministers following Kyiv’s strike on an Iranian vessel in the Caspian Sea. Tehran demanded compensation for the damage, while Kyiv blamed Russia for the incident and urged Iran to end support for Moscow’s war.

Ukraine Targets E-Commerce Giant Wildberries Again, Strikes Ryazan Oil Refinery in Latest Drone Wave — On Wednesday, Ukraine launched another wave of drone strikes deep inside Russia, hitting a Wildberries logistics hub and a major oil refinery in Ryazan, according to Russian officials and Ukrainian monitoring channels. The attack marks another strike on the Russian retail giant’s facilities amid an expanding campaign against Moscow’s logistics network.

Second Car Explodes in Odesa in One Day, Killing Driver and Injuring Passenger — A moving vehicle exploded in Odesa on Tuesday, killing its driver and injuring a passenger. The blast was the second car explosion in the city that day; the SBU classified the earlier incident as a terrorist attack.

Trump Envoys Witkoff, Kushner to Make First Kyiv Visit Following Zelensky-Trump Meeting — Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will make their first visit to Kyiv after repeatedly traveling to Moscow, following Zelensky’s hour-long meeting with Trump at the White House.

Zelensky Warns Trump Russia Is Preparing 30,000 More North Korean Troops for War Against Ukraine — Zelensky warned Washington that Russia is preparing to receive 30,000 additional North Korean troops and more ballistic missile launchers, arguing that Moscow’s reliance on foreign military partners poses a growing threat far beyond Ukraine.

US Senate Delivers Overwhelming 86-12 Bipartisan Backing for Russia Sanctions as Zelensky Watches — The US Senate voted 86–12 to advance sweeping sanctions targeting Russia’s energy revenues, financial networks and shadow fleet, delivering a powerful bipartisan show of support for Ukraine as Zelensky watched from the chamber.

Zelensky, Trump Hold ‘Positive’ White House Talks as US-Ukraine Ties Warm Over Patriots, Russia Pressure — Zelensky and Trump used their White House meeting to advance Patriot interceptor production, revive diplomacy with Russia and reinforce a broader strategy of military and economic pressure on Moscow.

‘Sick Man With a Gun’: Polish FM Warns ‘Desperate’ Putin Could Take Dangerous Risks — Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski warned that mounting economic and military pressure could make Vladimir Putin more dangerous, saying Russia’s capabilities are weaker than once believed but its intentions are “even worse.”

US Senate Begins Vote on Graham’s Russia Sanctions Bill as Zelensky Visits Washington — The US Senate is moving forward with sweeping Russia sanctions legislation championed by the late Lindsey Graham, targeting Moscow’s energy revenues, financial networks and countries that continue buying Russian oil and gas. The vote coincides with Zelensky’s visit to Washington for Graham’s funeral, meetings with US President Donald Trump and talks with US lawmakers.

Ukraine Reports 226 Combat Clashes, 29 Attacks Near Pokrovsk on Tuesday — The General Staff of Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) reported 226 combat clashes across the front on Tuesday, July 28 alone, with the heaviest fighting recorded near Pokrovsk, where 32 Russian soldiers were killed and 296 drones destroyed.

Sybiha Says Ukraine Wants to Avoid Escalation With Iran — Ukraine’s Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha held a phone call with his Iranian counterpart, seeking to avoid escalation after Kyiv struck an Iranian vessel in the Caspian Sea, killing one sailor.

Ukraine Discusses Joint Weapons Production With Lockheed Martin — President Volodymyr Zelensky met with Lockheed Martin representatives to discuss expanding joint weapons production and technology sharing. The talks focused on Patriot interceptor systems and other equipment, such as F-16, HIMARS, and ATACMS, critical to Ukraine’s defense.

Zelensky Marks Olenivka Anniversary, Confirms 9,613 Prisoners of War Freed — President Volodymyr Zelensky honored victims of the Olenivka prison camp killings on Tuesday, July 28, where more than 50 Ukrainian prisoners of war (POWs) died. He said 9,613 people have been returned from Russian captivity since the beginning of Russia’s war in 2022, although thousands more still remain under captivity.

Zelensky Meets With Trump, Discusses Patriot Missile Production — President Volodymyr Zelensky met with US President Donald Trump in the Oval Office on July 28, where the two discussed Patriot interceptor production licenses and ways to deepen strategic, diplomatic efforts toward peace.

Russians Form Street Patrol to Shield Men From Forced Recruitment — Residents of the Penza region settlement formed a 250-person civilian patrol to shield their men after recruiters allegedly beat and coerced locals into signing military contracts. The forced recruitment comes as Russia braces for expanded mobilization amid mounting battlefield losses, with Vladimir Putin pledging military spending will remain the Kremlin’s top budget priority through 2029.

US Senators Reach Deal on Russia, Iran Sanctions Bill — US senators unveiled a bipartisan sanctions bill targeting Russia and Iran that would allow President Donald Trump to impose tariffs on major buyers of Russian energy and extend sanctions against Tehran.

Zelensky Picks the Chairs, Loomer in Kyiv, Brovdi and Brzezinski — Ukraine's front lines held steady this week, with heavy fighting in Pokrovsk, Kostyantynivka, and Dobropillya, where a Russian armored push near Shakhove was destroyed within hours. Russia escalated economic warfare, striking Ukrainian cargo ships and Nova Poshta warehouses in retaliation for Ukraine's devastating drone campaign against Wildberries and Crimea's power grid. Zelensky replaced Syrsky with Drapaty as commander-in-chi

Ukraine Sees No Official Evidence of Iranian Missile Strike Plans — Ukraine's Center for Countering Disinformation said there is no official evidence Iran is preparing missile strikes against Ukraine, although Tehran possesses weapons capable of carrying out such attacks.

Ukraine’s New Defense Minister Hits Up the US, Germany and Britain for Help vs. Russian Missiles — New Defense Minister Khmara spent his first week on the job talking with allies to shore up Ukraine’s defense against ballistic missiles amid a shortage of Patriot PAC-3 interceptors; but despite more cordiality, discussions yielded no new agreement with the Trump administration on air defense help.

Russians Rush to Rent Apartments in Armenia Amid Mobilization Fears — Russians have sharply increased demand for apartments in Armenia's capital Yerevan amid rumors of a new mobilization wave, local realtors told Russian outlet Verstka on Tuesday. Rental prices in Yerevan have risen about 30% over the past three months, with one realtor saying the situation is "comparable to 2022." LIVE: Zelensky Meets Trump as Ukraine War Meets Iran War — Zelensky is set to meet Trump during his visit to the US at 9:30 a.m. local time as the US’s war in Iran becomes intertwined with Russia’s war in Ukraine.

Kyrgyzstan Seeks More Russian Fuel as Moscow’s Crisis Spreads Into Central Asia — Kyrgyzstan is reportedly in talks with Russia over additional fuel imports as Moscow’s fuel crisis spills into the Central Asian nation, which sources around 90% of its gasoline from Russia. Although Russia’s fuel export ban is due to expire at the end of July, its deputy prime minister has indicated it will likely be extended through the end of 2026.

Russian Navy's New Yasen-M Class Perm Submarine to Integrate Zircon Cruise Missiles — Russia said it is going to commission its new submarine, Perm, by the end of 2026, where it comes pre-equipped with launchers for the Zircon missiles – the same missiles that saw increased use in recent air raids against Ukrainian cities as Russia exploits Kyiv’s Patriot missile shortage.

Two Men Face Prison After Brutal Attack on Ukrainian Couple in Poland’s Wrocław — Two men arrested over the brutal assault of a Ukrainian couple in Poland’s Wrocław face up to five years in prison as prosecutors investigate a possible hate crime. A third suspect remains at large after the attack, which left both victims hospitalized with suspected concussions.

Russian Fuel Crisis 'Stabilizing' as Refineries 'Operational Again,' Kremlin's Deputy PM Novak Claims — Russia’s Deputy PM Alexander Novak reassured the country that refineries are slowly returning to operations and the fuel crisis is going to improve soon – though earlier reports suggest that even without new Ukrainian strikes, 40 percent of refineries struck are unlikely to resume operations within the next two months.

Russia, North Korea Near Completion of First Road Bridge Amid War Supply Concerns — Russia and North Korea are close to completing their first-ever road bridge, a crossing over the Tumen River, that Ukrainian investigators say is designed to serve as a covert military logistics corridor rather than boost trade. Road transport is harder to monitor via satellite than rail, making it easier to move troops, weapons, and military officials discreetly, giving both parties an advantage.

WATCH: Ukrainian Drone Interceptors Down Rare Russian Forpost-R UAV Over Kursk Region — Ukraine’s drone forces shot down a rare Russian Forpost-R strike and reconnaissance UAV over the Kursk region using a domestically developed interceptor drone. The high-value aircraft was destroyed at an altitude of 14,100 feet, marking only the sixth confirmed loss of the model since Russia’s full-scale invasion.

Zelensky Won’t Bring Fedorov Back Despite Protests, Insiders Say — Zelensky is reportedly unwilling to reinstate former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov despite continuing “cardboard protests.” Organizers are considering a march in Kyiv on Friday, while presidential insiders expect the demonstrations to eventually lose momentum.

Pentagon to Stretch $400M Ukraine Aid Until Trump Leaves Office — The Trump administration has told Congress it will not complete spending $400 million authorized for Ukraine aid until fiscal year 2029 – the year Trump leaves office – even as Kyiv faces critical weapons shortages. The Pentagon sent lawmakers a letter outlining the timeline in May, but the funds remain unspent and not put on contract.

Trump Says US Will Verify Zelensky's Claim on Russia-Iran Satellite Sharing — US President Donald Trump said the US will check President Volodymyr Zelensky’s claim that Russia had shared satellite images of American bases with Iran, but argued that – even if it’s true – it will have no real impact on Iran’s military capabilities.

Russian Strikes Leave Kharkiv-Poltava Route Without Fuel Stations — Russian strikes may have destroyed more than 80 petrol stations across Kharkiv Oblast, leaving the entire Kharkiv-Poltava stretch of the motorway without a single working fuel stop. Ukrainian authorities say the campaign fits a wider pattern of Russian strikes on civilian logistics.

Ukraine Could Strike Moscow With Homegrown Ballistic Missiles This Autumn, Developer Says — Ukraine could launch its first ballistic missile strikes on Moscow as early as this autumn, the head of defense company Fire Point said. The developer claims testing of a new missile system is nearing completion, with Ukraine preparing to deploy domestically produced weapons against targets inside Russia.

Honoring Senator Lindsey Graham – Helping Ukraine, Punishing Russia — With the US Congress poised to vote on a Russian sanctions package cosponsored by the late Senator Lindsey Graham, President Zelensky’s visit to the US and Donald Trump’s Oval Office could signal a turning point.

New Zealand Intelligence Casts Doubt on Russia Spy Accusation — Russia’s FSB claims it uncovered a New Zealand-linked espionage operation after arresting a Russian man accused of passing sensitive information to Wellington. New Zealand dismissed Russian state media as an unreliable source, while experts said the allegations should be treated with skepticism amid already strained bilateral ties.

Zelensky Arrives in US for Oval Office Talks With Trump — President Volodymyr Zelensky will meet US President Donald Trump in the Oval Office on Tuesday as Ukraine seeks stronger air defenses and deeper strategic cooperation. Zelensky will also attend a Washington memorial service for the late Republican Senator Lindsey Graham.

Pentagon Admits US Drone Production Remains Far Behind Ukraine — Ukraine is expected to produce 6 to 7 million FPV drones this year, while the Pentagon plans to order fewer than 200,000 by February under its $1.1 billion Drone Dominance program.

Moscow Hit by Massive Drone Raid as Russia Claims Over 390 UAVs Launched — A large drone attack disrupted Moscow early Tuesday, forcing airport restrictions as Russian authorities claimed dozens of UAVs were intercepted near the capital.
Trump to Host Zelensky at White House as US-Russia Diplomacy Stalls — White House Confirms Time for Trump-Zelensky Meeting Tuesday

All 100 Senators Invited to Meet Zelensky as Washington Signals Shift in Ukraine Policy – Why It Matters — Zelensky’s Senate outreach comes as Washington weighs tougher sanctions on Russia, deeper defense co-production and a broader shift in how the US supports Ukraine.

UK’s New PM Burnham Pledges ‘100%’ Support for Ukraine, as Zelensky heads to Trump Talks — British Prime Minister Andy Burnham made Zelensky his first foreign leader meeting, pledging continuity in UK support and transferring Stone Cloak electronic warfare technology for Ukrainian production ahead of the president’s Washington visit.

4 Killed, 18 Wounded in Russian Attacks Across Donetsk Region – Infant Among Injured — Four civilians were killed and 18 others wounded, including an 11-month-old baby, in Russian attacks across Donetsk region on July 27, according to regional prosecutors.

Romania Expels Russian Diplomat After Repeated Drone Incursions — Romania ordered a Russian embassy employee to leave the country within five days after NATO fighter jets shot down three stray drones over the weekend. One of the downed drones was confirmed to be a Russian-made Shahed model.

Zelensky Keeps Silent on Fedorov’s Possible Reappointment — Zelensky has refused to say whether he could reappoint former Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, merely saying he could not frequently intervene in disputes between the defense ministry and the military before saying he respected both Fedorov and Syrsky.

Romania Spent €1.5 Million Downing Russian Drones — Romania spent about €1.5 million to shoot down three Russian drones that entered its airspace in three days, exposing the high cost of defending NATO borders and fuelling efforts to deploy more affordable counter-drone systems.

Russia Arrests Man Accused of Spying for New Zealand — Russia's FSB claimed to have caught a 55-year-old man spying for New Zealand by initially volunteering his services. Footage of his arrest shows wads of US dollars and tiny tank models inside his apartment, but no screenshots of his direct messages to New Zealand despite the FSB’s claims.

Small Packages, Bigger Impact? EU Reportedly Eyes New Russia Sanctions Approach — The EU is reportedly considering dropping its current sanctions package approach against Russia by either breaking measures into smaller packages or adopting them at lower levels, after Greece’s veto to protect the interests of a shipping company transporting Russian LNG delayed the latest package and arguably made the measures weaker than before the latest package’s adoption.

Lithuania Proposes Entry Ban for Pro-War Russians, Belarusians — Lithuania's foreign ministry proposed new sanctions that would bar Russian and Belarusian supporters of the war against Ukraine from entering the country and restrict property purchases near strategic facilities.

Russia's Wildberries Takes Down War Product Page After Ukrainian Strikes — Russia’s Wildberries has reportedly removed the listings from its “Everything for the SVO” page following repeated Ukrainian strikes that set several of its warehouses ablaze, as affected business owners pleaded for assistance after the company previously refused to compensate them for their losses.

Kazakhstan Calls on Putin to Freeze the War — Kazakhstan’s President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev publicly urged Vladimir Putin to freeze the war in Ukraine, saying its causes were incomprehensible. Commentators described the remarks as a rare public challenge to Putin’s justification for the invasion, while arguing that the Kremlin is unlikely to change course voluntarily because it views accepting Ukraine’s sovereignty as a defeat.

‘We Did Not Start Any War’: Putin Again Denies Russia’s Responsibility for Ukraine Invasion — Putin once again claimed Russia was not responsible for starting the war against Ukraine, saying Moscow only “responded” to Kyiv. The Russian leader repeated his claims about Ukraine’s history and said Moscow was restoring what he called a “historical course.”

Organizer of Deadly Kyiv Defense Exhibition Held for 60 Days After Russian Strike — A Kyiv court ordered 60 days of pretrial detention for Vasyl Honcharuk, the organizer of a defense exhibition that was struck by two Russian ballistic missiles on July 24. Eleven people were killed, while dozens were wounded.

Cargo Vessel Lethally-Hit by Russian Anti-Ship Missiles Sinks Near Odesa Port — The cargo ship Golden Leo, crippled by a Russian missile strike a week earlier that killed 10 people, finally sank near Odesa on Sunday after days adrift. The loss came amid escalating Russian and Ukrainian attacks on civilian Black Sea shipping.

‘I Truly Believe This Is Urgent’: MAGA Ally Loomer Urges US to Send Patriots to Ukraine — MAGA commentator Laura Loomer called on the US to supply Ukraine with additional Patriot missiles after witnessing Russian missile attacks in Kyiv, arguing the systems would protect civilians while also serving American security interests.

Zelensky Updates Targets for Long-Range Strikes on Russia — Zelensky said Ukraine updated its list of priority targets for long-range strikes against Russia after more than 1,000 missions this year. He said the campaign aims to weaken Russia’s military production, logistics and economy while pushing Moscow toward diplomacy.

Putin Plans to Send Up to 500,000 More Russians to War, Zelensky Warns — President Volodymyr Zelensky said Russia was preparing to mobilize between 300,000 and 500,000 people in late September or early October. He urged Ukraine’s allies to impose stronger sanctions and disrupt Russia’s fuel, weapons and logistics networks before the reported call-up begins.

Russia Fires ‘Factory-Fresh’ Missiles at Ukraine, Air Force Says — Ukraine said markings on recently launched Russian missiles indicated they had been manufactured within the past few months. The number of missiles launched in July also exceeded estimates of what Moscow would need to maintain its stockpile, while the share of ballistic missiles used rose significantly compared with cruise missiles.

SBU Detains FSB Agents Accused of Plotting to Poison Ukrainian Soldiers at ‘Charity’ Party — Ukraine’s Security Service (SBU) said it foiled an alleged Russian plot to kill dozens of Ukrainian soldiers by luring them to a fake charity party, where FSB agents planned to poison drinks and detonate a 10-kilogram bomb. Two suspects have been detained and face life imprisonment.

Zelensky Wants to Build Major Drone Factory in UK — Zelensky said Ukraine aims to build a large drone factory in the UK and expand bilateral defense cooperation through a new "drone deal." He also warned Russia is increasing ballistic missile production and urged allies to strengthen Ukraine's air defenses.

Russian Lawmakers Demand Europe Pay Compensation for Its War on Ukraine — Russian lawmakers said, that Moscow will demand compensation from European countries for damages caused by the war in Ukraine. Russia will also seek the return of $300 billion in frozen assets.

Iran Threatens Kyiv Again, Warns of ‘Unforeseen’ Consequences After Attack on Caspian Sea Ship — Iran has threatened “unforeseen” consequences after Ukraine said it carried out strikes on vessels in the Caspian Sea carrying military cargo linked to Iran. Tehran called the attack illegal and vowed Kyiv would be held accountable after reporting casualties aboard an Iranian ship.

Zelensky Fires Back at Iran’s Threat: ‘You Already Attacked Ukraine’ — President Volodymyr Zelensky rejected Iran’s claim of noninvolvement in the war, pointing to its military support for Russia. His comments came after Tehran warned that Ukraine’s strike on an Iranian vessel in the Caspian Sea “cannot go unanswered.”

Ukraine Targets Russia’s Strategic Maritime Hub, State Fuel Depot in Deep Drone Raid — On Monday, Ukraine launched overnight drone strikes targeting Russia’s Rostov Sea Trade Port and a strategic state fuel depot in Udmurtia, about 1,350 kilometers from the Ukrainian border, according to OSINT analysts. Russia also reported casualties and damage in Rostov-on-Don and Belgorod following the attacks.

UK’s Burnham to Welcome Zelensky in First Foreign Leader Visit — Zelensky heads to London to meet new UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham as Britain doubles down on its backing for Ukraine. The talks come ahead of his Washington visit, with defence ties, drone cooperation and new battlefield technology at the center of discussions as Kyiv seeks more weapons to counter Russia’s attacks.

Kremlin Shrugs Off Reports of US-Ukraine Air Truce Plan, Says It’s ‘Too Early’ — The Kremlin dismissed reports that Washington and Kyiv are preparing a proposal for a partial aerial ceasefire, saying it is too early to comment. Reuters reports the plan is part of a broader US-backed peace package that could be presented to Moscow as diplomatic efforts gain momentum.

Russian Overnight Strikes Kill One, Injure Dozens Across Ukraine — Russia launched overnight attacks across Ukraine, killing a man and injuring at least 12 civilians in Zaporizhzhia, Sumy, and Dnipropetrovsk regions. A guided bomb destroyed a home, while air defenses shot down 15 drones over the Dnipropetrovsk region.

Russia Preparing For 30,000 More North Korean Troops, Zelensky Warns — Zelensky said North Korea is preparing to send more ballistic missile launchers to Russia, warning Moscow is helping Pyongyang improve its weapons through combat experience. He also claimed Russia plans a new mobilization this fall after suffering more than 225,000 casualties so far this year.
